16:15 — The Safe Place, Kitchen & Roof Stairs

Pony

Something in the Safe Place kitchen smells like a melted bicycle tyre, which means Giraffy lost another bet to Mimi and is paying it off by cooking dinner.

Pony pushes his round wire-framed glasses up his nose, peers cautiously around the doorway into the converted ground-floor dining room, and watches two metres of enthusiastic giraffe stir a pot of pale orange paste with a wooden spoon that is visibly smoking at the tip.

"Giraffy," Pony says evenly, leaning one shoulder against the doorframe. "Why is the spoon smoking? Water boils at one hundred degrees. Wood doesn't char at one hundred degrees."

"Aha! Good eye, Pony!" Giraffy booms cheerfully, nearly braining himself on the hanging copper pan rack as he turns around in his singed novelty apron. "It's roasted butternut and rosemary! I just added a tiny splash of sunflower oil to the bottom first so it wouldn't stick, and then the stove dial got a little excited!"

"You turned the burner up to nine and walked away to water your kale on the roof," Pony deadpans. "Didn't you."

Giraffy's ears droop. "Maybe."

"How long were you gone?"

"Ten minutes? Twelve? The kale needed me, Pony."

Mimi's voice drifts down the roof stairs. "He was gone for forty minutes!"

"Traitor," Giraffy whispers.

Pony sighs and reaches past him to turn the dial down. "Open the window. I'll get the fire blanket."

"You're a hero," Giraffy says. "A small, judgemental hero."

"I'm the same height as you when you sit down."

"That's true," Giraffy admits. "That's very true."
